title: Fold a batch of plays into episode counters
prompt:
A podcast app keeps running totals per episode in episode_stats. Every few minutes the raw plays that arrived since the last run land in play_batch, one row per play.

Write SQL that folds play_batch into episode_stats. For an episode that already has a row, add the new plays and seconds and move last_played forward. For an episode with no row yet, insert one.

- The check runs SELECT episode_id, plays, seconds_listened, last_played FROM episode_stats
- plays grows by the number of batch rows for the episode
- seconds can be NULL (the client did not report it); such a play still counts but adds 0 seconds
- last_played becomes the later of the stored date and the newest played_on in the batch; a stored NULL counts as no date
- One episode can appear many times in the batch
- Any row order is fine
hints: Insert-or-update in one statement is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (episode_id) DO UPDATE. Inside DO UPDATE, EXCLUDED is the row you tried to insert.
If the batch has two rows for one episode, a single upsert would try to update the same row twice, which Postgres rejects. Aggregate the batch per episode first.

INSERT INTO episode_stats AS s SELECT episode_id, count(*), coalesce(sum(seconds), 0), max(played_on) FROM play_batch GROUP BY episode_id ON CONFLICT (episode_id) DO UPDATE SET plays = s.plays + EXCLUDED.plays, ... last_played = greatest(s.last_played, EXCLUDED.last_played);

exercise.schema:
CREATE TABLE episode_stats (episode_id int PRIMARY KEY, plays int NOT NULL, seconds_listened int NOT NULL, last_played date);
CREATE TABLE play_batch (id int PRIMARY KEY, episode_id int NOT NULL, seconds int, played_on date NOT NULL);
exercise.solution:
INSERT INTO episode_stats AS s (episode_id, plays, seconds_listened, last_played)
SELECT episode_id, count(*), coalesce(sum(seconds), 0), max(played_on)
FROM play_batch
GROUP BY episode_id
ON CONFLICT (episode_id) DO UPDATE
SET plays = s.plays + EXCLUDED.plays,
    seconds_listened = s.seconds_listened + EXCLUDED.seconds_listened,
    last_played = greatest(s.last_played, EXCLUDED.last_played);
exercise.check: SELECT episode_id, plays, seconds_listened, last_played FROM episode_stats;

hiddenTests.name: plays with NULL seconds

INSERT INTO play_batch VALUES (1, 1, NULL, '2026-02-02'), (2, 1, NULL, '2026-02-03'), (3, 4, NULL, '2026-02-03');

hiddenTests.name: stored last_played is NULL
hiddenTests.seed:

hiddenTests.name: mix of NULL and real seconds
hiddenTests.seed:
INSERT INTO episode_stats VALUES (2, 1, 15, '2026-06-01');
INSERT INTO play_batch VALUES (1, 2, NULL, '2026-06-02'), (2, 2, 45, '2026-06-02');

explanation: Aggregating the batch first gives one candidate row per episode, so ON CONFLICT can update each stored row at most once; feeding raw rows fails with 'ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time'. count(*) counts plays even when seconds is NULL, while count(seconds) would undercount. sum(seconds) is NULL when every value is NULL, and adding NULL would wipe the total, so coalesce it to 0. greatest() ignores NULL arguments in Postgres, so it handles both a stored NULL and late-arriving plays.
notes: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT is atomic per row, so concurrent batches cannot both insert the same episode; one waits for the other and then takes the DO UPDATE path. Concurrent batches touching the same episodes can deadlock if they lock rows in different orders, so adding ORDER BY episode_id to the SELECT is a cheap safeguard. In production you would also delete or mark the batch rows in the same transaction, for example with a data-modifying CTE (WITH moved AS (DELETE FROM play_batch RETURNING *) ...).
followUps: How would you make the job safe to re-run if it crashes after the upsert but before the batch is cleared?
When would you prefer MERGE over INSERT ... ON CONFLICT here?
